summary: Weekly pilot sync focusing on Dedicated sizing and autoscaling policies. Reviewed last week's benchmark preliminary numbers (p50/p95 token latency, throughput), discussed burst versus sustained capacity, autoscale thresholds, warm pool vs cold start behavior, and network/KMS/security requirements. Action items: update sizing spreadsheet with burst scenarios, run extended benchmark with Atlas traffic, and share security docs. Agreed to run a 2-hour benchmark next week and reconvene after results.
topics: Dedicated sizing and GPU pool planning
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, um it's the weekly sync for the POC — quick roll call?
[00:12] Samantha Cole: hi all, Samantha here.
[00:15] Diego Martinez: Diego on from infra.
[00:18] Aaron Zhao: Aaron, security.
[00:20] Lina Park: Lina, product.
[00:22] Priya Desai: priya from redwood, se.
[00:24] Marco Liu: marco, csm.
[00:26] Jordan Kim: cool, thanks. Quick agenda: sizing review, autoscale rules, burst planning, and then benchmarks & next steps. ok?
[00:32] Samantha Cole: yep, go ahead.
[00:35] Priya Desai: alright, so we pulled the preliminary numbers from the last benchmark you shared. we ran the model on dedicated nodes with the baseline config: 4x A100-ish type GPUs — note, the runtime shows as Redwood Dedicate in the logs, sometimes transcribed as "red wood dedicate" but it's the dedicated runtime. our p50 token latency averaged around 40ms and p95 around 220ms at 500 qps simulated. that was with batching window of 25ms and continuous KV cache warm for session affinity.
[01:05] Diego Martinez: uh quick question, 500 qps sustained or burst?
[01:08] Priya Desai: that was sustained for 15 minutes in the test ramp. we also did a 30-second burst test to 1.2k qps — saw p95 jump to about 520ms on the smaller instance pool because of cold-starts on new workers.
[01:22] Samantha Cole: so that cold-start hit is our concern — real traffic has spikes around promo windows where qps doubles for a couple minutes.
[01:29] Jordan Kim: totally, and that's why we wanted to talk through autoscale policies: cooldowns, pre-warm pools, and burst capacity. Priya, can you walk through recommended policy?
[01:38] Priya Desai: yeah. recommended pattern: maintain a small warm pool — 10-15% headroom — plus autoscale based on 95th percentile CPU/GPU utilization with a short reaction tier for bursts. specifically: scale-up threshold at GPU util > 70% for 20s, scale-up step of +2 workers, cooldown 60s; scale-down threshold < 40% for 120s, step -1. for promo bursts we suggest enabling a burst capacity reservation — reserved instances that can be used for 5-10 minutes before spilling to on-demand. that avoids high p95 during short spikes.
[02:19] Diego Martinez: reserved instances for bursts, is that the dedicated burst bucket you mentioned earlier? how does billing look — we are sensitive to cost.
[02:27] Jordan Kim: yes it's the burst bucket. billing depends on reserved vs on-demand; the burst reservation is like a short-term capacity add-on — you pay for reserved minutes at a lower rate than on-demand, but higher than long-term reserved. we can model costs in the sizing sheet. i'll update with cost columns.
[02:45] Lina Park: another question — do you support per-route SLOs? we want checkout flows to have tighter latency guarantees.
[02:51] Priya Desai: yes, per-route configs: you can pin the checkout route to a lower-latency model variant, or route to a higher-priority pool in the dedicated cluster. it also supports canary routing and fallbacks — e.g., if the low-latency variant is overloaded, fall back to a cheaper variant with slightly higher latency but still within acceptable range.
[03:12] Aaron Zhao: re security, we need to confirm KMS integration and audit logs for all inference calls. any gaps?
[03:18] Marco Liu: we'll share our SOC2 artifacts and the KMS config notes — there shouldn't be gaps for the dedicated offering, we support customer-managed keys, and all request logs are available in the console with export. marco will send network diagram as well.
[03:32] Diego Martinez: cool. can you also include the expected VPC peering steps? our networking folks will need that.
[03:36] Marco Liu: yes, we'll include peering steps and a template.
[03:40] Priya Desai: back to sizing — we also tested quantized model variant which reduced memory pressure and allowed denser packing: same throughput with 25% fewer workers but with a 10-15% increase in p95 in some prompts. so tradeoff: cost vs tail latency.
[03:58] Samantha Cole: interesting, that might be ok for some routes but not checkout.
[04:02] Jordan Kim: exactly, that's where per-route model assignment helps.
[04:06] Diego Martinez: for the burst scenario, what about warm start time? you mentioned cold starts caused p95 spikes. what is the typical bootstrap time for a new worker?
[04:15] Priya Desai: cold init for a worker with a 30b quantized model is about 14-22s to become fully ready; with pre-warmed container images it drops to ~6-8s. KV cache warming for session context takes longer depending on request mix — that's why we prefer to keep a minimal warm pool to absorb short spikes.
[04:36] Aaron Zhao: any requirement for fetching model weights from an external registry that could affect warm start?
[04:41] Priya Desai: weights are typically cached on local instance store; in private deployments we can pre-stage artifacts. in hosted, we keep a shared artifact cache. if you have air-gapped needs, we can do on-prem packages but that adds setup time.
[04:56] Samantha Cole: ok, next piece: we looked at the sizing spreadsheet you shared. Diego, can you confirm the baseline qps patterns?
[05:03] Diego Martinez: baseline daily average is around 300 qps, p95 spikes to 900 occasionally during promos. checkout route is ~30% of traffic during peak.
[05:12] Jordan Kim: thanks. so Priya, in the sizing calc spreadsheet can you run scenarios: (A) sustained 500 qps, (B) burst to 1.5k qps for 2 minutes, (C) sustained 300 qps + promo spikes to 900 for 5 minutes — and show GPU counts, cost, and expected p95 for each?
[05:32] Priya Desai: yes we'll add those. We'll also include a scenario with a pre-warmed burst pool of 2 workers.
[05:39] Lina Park: regarding SLA, what sort of latency SLO can we expect for pinned checkout routes?
[05:44] Jordan Kim: typically for pinned high-priority pools we can target p95 < 200-250ms depending on model size; for smaller models it's lower. exact SLOs depend on the model and quantization. we'll include ranges in the sheet.
[05:57] Samantha Cole: can we also simulate real user traffic pattern rather than uniform qps? the promo spikes are overlaid on a diurnal curve.
[06:03] Priya Desai: absolutely. for the benchmark next week we'll replay trace-based traffic you provide. that'll give us better tail behavior visibility.
[06:10] Diego Martinez: we can provide a 48-hour trace with anonymized payloads.
[06:14] Jordan Kim: perfect. Priya, you mentioned autoscale cooldowns earlier — could you explain why you chose 60s/120s numbers?
[06:21] Priya Desai: sure — it's balancing sensitivity vs thrash. scale-up needs to be responsive so shorter observation windows (20s) catch sharp increases; cooldown 60s avoids spinning up too many workers in noisy signals. scale-down is conservative (120s) to avoid dropping capacity prematurely during short troughs. we also allow step-scaling to add capacity in chunks.
[06:45] Samantha Cole: and rate limiting at the route level — can Redwood apply token-bucket throttling to protect backend? we might prefer backpressure over added cost.
[06:53] Priya Desai: yes per-route rate-limits and queueing policies exist. you can set a token bucket per route or global. queue time windows also configurable, we can fail-fast for checkout route rather than queue too long.
[07:05] Diego Martinez: what about priority pre-emption? can checkout jobs pre-empt background inference?
[07:10] Priya Desai: yes with multi-tenant pools you can set priority classes; higher priority requests get scheduled first and background requests can be delayed or routed to cheaper variants.
[07:19] Jordan Kim: okay shifting to benchmarks: we propose a 2-hour run on Wednesday 2026-03-25 where we replay your 48-hour trace at 2x speed to compress into the window, and include burst simulations. agrees?
[07:32] Samantha Cole: that works. Diego will provide trace by EOD Monday.
[07:36] Diego Martinez: yep, i'll upload the trace and anonymize payloads.
[07:39] Marco Liu: i'll set up the benchmark job and provide the runbook so you can reproduce locally if needed.
[07:44] Aaron Zhao: security-wise, the benchmark will include synthetic payloads only, right? we won't upload PII.
[07:49] Diego Martinez: correct, it'll be anonymized.
[07:52] Priya Desai: next, on the subject of metrics: we'll publish p50/p90/p95/p99 plus GPU util, memory pressure, and call-level logs with a sampling rate. we'll include distributed traces for checkout route.
[08:06] Samantha Cole: can you also provide cost delta between pre-warming 2 workers vs paying for on-demand scale-ups during spikes?
[08:12] Jordan Kim: yep that's part of the sizing sheet — cost columns will show reserved-minute costs vs on-demand.
[08:19] Lina Park: for private deployments — any blockers? we need to confirm VPC peering and KMS access.
[08:25] Marco Liu: private deployment is ready; we'll provide a step-by-step. KMS integration requires a short handoff with your security team to rotate keys and set IAM roles. estimated setup time 2-3 weeks if we do a dedicated private install.
[08:40] Aaron Zhao: that timeline is fine as long as the POC can run in hosted dedicated for now.
[08:45] Jordan Kim: yes hosted Dedicated should satisfy this POC while private deployment is scoped.
[08:49] Samantha Cole: about monitoring retention — can we keep logs for 90 days?
[08:53] Marco Liu: default retention is 30 days; we offer add-on retention tiers up to 365 days. we'll include pricing for 90-day retention.
[09:02] Priya Desai: any other technical risks? we noted the KV-cache behavior might cause increased p95 when many new sessions arrive; to mitigate we recommend session affinity or sticky routing to workers with cache warm.
[09:15] Diego Martinez: sticky sessions are fine for us.
[09:18] Jordan Kim: good. quick recap before closing: Jordan will update sizing spreadsheet with the three scenarios + cost columns and burst reservation calc; Priya will run the 2-hour benchmark (Wed 3/25) using Diego's trace; Marco to send SOC2/KMS/network docs; Diego to upload trace by Monday; Atlas to confirm pilot end date & success criteria by 3/30.
[09:43] Samantha Cole: sounds good.
[09:45] Lina Park: thanks all.
[09:47] Jordan Kim: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the calendar invite for the benchmark and updated sheet. bye.
[09:53] (recording ends)
